note: A cohort study of 95 fetuses with isolated horseshoe kidney identified 1 case with a pathogenic PSMD12 variant (1/95 or 1/45 by exome sequencing, ~1-2%), and PSMD12 haploinsufficiency causes syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder (Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome).

evidence.text: In a cohort of 95 fetuses diagnosed with isolated horseshoe kidney where 45 underwent trio exome sequencing, one case (1/95, ~1.1%, or 1/45, 2.2%) had a causative c.796-1G > A variant in PSMD12.

source.title: Clinically Significant Genetic Results in Fetuses With Isolated Horseshoe Kidney
source.quote: Among the cases that yielded negative results from CMA, 45 proceeded to trio ES. Notably, two disease-causing variants, c.796-1G > A in PSMD12 and c.11707 C > T (p.Gln3903*) in KMT2D, were detected in each case.

evidence.text: PSMD12 haploinsufficiency causes Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome, characterized by developmental delay/intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphism, and variable congenital malformations including renal anomalies.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: Haploinsufficiency of PSMD12 has been reported in individuals with neurodevelopmental phenotypes, including developmental delay/intellectual disability (DD/ID), facial dysmorphism, and congenital malformations, defined as Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS).
